business_model.assessment: Mightylicious sells packaged gluten-free/vegan cookies, flour blends and brownie mix through direct-to-consumer online, wholesale and retail channels [A27, A28]. Payers are consumers and retailers/wholesale customers, buying one-time per order; no subscription or contract revenue is documented. Revenue is $459,216 in FY2025, up about 32% from $347,602 in FY2024 [A18, B2]. Cost of goods sold exceeded revenue in both years (gross loss of $29,477 in FY2025 [A19] and $117,069 in FY2024 [B1]), so unit economics are not yet shown to be positive. The issuer says vertical integration should lower COGS [B7], but no cost, timeline or evidence is given. The Form C does not split revenue by channel or customer. The reviewed notes contain boilerplate that does not fit a cookie business (customers 'prepay for services at the time of booking') [B6], which lowers confidence in the care taken with the statements.

competition.assessment: The issuer names four competitors: Aliea's, Tate's Bake Shop, Dr. Schar and Udi's, and says it competes with many large and small companies, including well-known global competitors [A29]. Differentiation is limited to product attributes (gluten-free, vegan, kosher, Non-GMO, taste, Gen X/Millennial target) [A27]. The pack gives no market share, pricing, margin comparison or customer-switching evidence. Risk factors name shelf-space competition, retailers' negotiating power and better-resourced competitors [A29]. Two trademarks are registered, but no patent or other durable moat is documented. Competitive position is therefore asserted, not demonstrated.

demand_evidence.assessment: Documented demand is real but modest: reviewed revenue of $459,216 (FY2025) and $347,602 (FY2024) [A18]. The reviewed statements are not audited and sales are not tied to named contracts [A24]. Stronger traction statements ('$100K MoM run rate', '1800 doors in over 49 states', Kroger/Giant/HEB/HyVee, Amazon +355% YoY) appear only in an undated testing-the-waters email, with no basis or period [A32]. They are not reconciled to FY2025 revenue of $459,216, so they are issuer assertions only. The email also says the higher run rate 'accelerated our cash burn' [B8]. Retailer contracts, purchase orders, channel revenue and any 2026 interim financials are missing from the pack. Wakefern and Wegmans launches are described as pending or Q4 2026 plans, not completed events [A32].

economics_and_funding.assessment: Reviewed FY2025 figures (year ended 2025-12-31, about 9.5 months before the cutoff): net loss $896,217, operating cash outflow $960,595, cash $116,414 plus $1,397,792 in marketable securities at that date [A20, A25, A21]. Total liabilities were $5,354,602, mostly SAFEs carried at $5,007,597 [A22, A23], leaving a stockholders' deficit of $(3,507,862). The accountant's report includes a going-concern paragraph [A24]. The issuer states $654,000 in cash and equivalents at 2026-06-30 and about 5 months of runway; this is an unreviewed issuer figure whose relationship to the Dec 2025 cash and securities is unexplained [A26]. I do not compute a current runway from these mismatched figures. Disclosed debt totals $139,475 (EIDL $80,000 secured by all assets, Wayflyer $51,000, CEO loans $8,475) [A17, B5]. The offering raises $75,000 minimum and $1,000,000 maximum [A5], and the issuer calls the proceeds 'essential to our operations' [A26]. Even the maximum is small against the FY2025 cash burn, and the issuer plans further capital raises [A26]. Intermediary fees and the onboarding fee reduce net proceeds [A7].

execution_risks.assessment: Key risks: (1) continued losses, with COGS above revenue and a going-concern paragraph [A19, A24]; (2) dependence on a sole officer, with 2 employees and the CEO handling a wide range of administrative and operational functions [A30, B11]; (3) retail-expansion risks, with Wakefern/Wegmans launches pending and new retail growth needing working capital [A32]; (4) heavy reliance on third-party suppliers, co-packers and retailers, and exposure to commodity and tariff costs, per risk factors; (5) the proceeds plan differs between Form C and press release (vertical integration and executive hiring appear only in the press release) [B7]; (6) disclosure quality issues: boilerplate in the notes [B6], unreconciled traction claims [A32], a custodian-name mismatch [A35], and testing-the-waters materials that the issuer says 'may not have included proper disclaimers'. Availability is unverified: the platform page was not reachable, and the press release describing the campaign as live comes from the issuer [B13].

price_and_terms.assessment: The SAFE is sold at $1.00 per unit of purchase amount; the price is described as 'arbitrary', which is a disclosure rather than proof of mis-pricing [A4]. The operative reference is the $15,000,000 pre-money valuation cap [A9]. The cap sits against 1,000,000 outstanding shares, an implied cap price of $15 per share before SAFEs [B3]. The cap is about 32.7x FY2025 revenue (arithmetic only, with no comparables in the pack) [B12]. There is no discount in the cited terms. Existing SAFEs with principal of $5,096,791 also carry a $15,000,000 cap, and equal about 34% of the cap [A15, B4]. They convert on top of this offering because SAFEs are excluded from the denominator [A9]. K1 and K2 ($1,000,000 and $1,075,000) simply multiply the $1.00 SAFE unit price by share counts; the $1.00 is a purchase-amount unit, not a share price. These figures are not a valuation of the company and should not be read as such [B10]. K3 and K4 are withheld. Investor-side fees are not stated in the cited text. The Form C 'greater of' conversion wording differs from the SAFE form's Equity Financing Price definition [A9]. The SAFE form should govern.

security_path_to_proceeds.assessment: The security is a Crowd SAFE held through a custodian/nominee; investors hold a beneficial interest only [A35]. Routes to cash are separate questions. (a) Conversion: it happens only on an Equity Financing, defined as the next sale of Capital Stock for at least $1,000,000 gross cash; the SAFE sale itself is not a sale of Capital Stock, so this offering does not appear to trigger conversion [A9, B9]. The issuer discloses it may never conduct one and is under no obligation to convert otherwise [A13]. (b) Liquidity Event (IPO, direct listing, change of control) or Dissolution: a cash-out right exists, but it is junior to debt and creditor claims, on par with other SAFEs/preferred, and senior to common; payment is limited to available funds [A10]. The notes' description of dissolution priority differs [A10]. Existing SAFEs of $5,096,791 share this pari passu class [A15]. The EIDL loan has all-asset collateral [A17]. No waterfall beyond the SAFE form language is stated. (c) Transfer: a one-year Reg CF restriction applies, plus opinion-of-counsel and no-competitor limits; a legal ability to transfer does not mean a buyer exists [A12]. (d) No voting, information or anti-dilution rights [A11]. The CEO ('Lead') controls amendments and acts as proxy [A35]. No public market exists or is contemplated.

team_evidence.assessment: The only documented officer and director is founder-CEO Carolyn Haeler, who owns 100% of the 1,000,000 outstanding common shares [A16]. Her issuer-provided bio: Yale MBA, finance roles (J.P. Morgan asset management, a hedge fund, IBM supply-chain consulting), and founder of the business in 2017, with cookies on sale at Whole Foods by January 2018 [A30]. This shows 8+ years of operating the business, but it is self-reported and not independently verified. Her documented background is in finance and consulting, and no prior food-industry operating or manufacturing role is documented in the pack. The company has 2 employees [A30]. Advisors are mentioned without names [A30]. The press release says key executives will be hired with part of the raise [B7]; no named hires exist. Single-person dependence is the main team finding [B11].
